data.description: Crown rump length (CRL) is the length from the top of the head to bottom of the torso.
Length of the ear from the crown to the tip.

Comments associated with the specimen that are contributed by users of the collection. May or may not be part of the original documentation. Submitted to or collected by collection staff and subject to curatorial approval.
Width measurement of the bursa. Specify means of measurement in Methods.
The file format format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource following the National Archives Format Authority List.

In mineralogy, crystal habit is the characteristic external shape of an individual crystal or crystal group. A single crystal's habit is a description of its general shape and its crystallographic forms, and how well developed each form is.
Organs, cavities, surfaces, and locations examined for the possibility of parasites.
The ability or power to conduct or transmit heat, electricity, or sound through a substance.
Widest part of the narrow axis of a whole egg.
Weight measurement of the gonad (which may be testes or ovary and can be indicated in Remarks or by implication of attribute of sex). Left or right side gonad should be indicated in the Methods.
Total length of the femur, tibia/fibula, tarsals, metatarsals and toes.
Is the object framed? Yes or No.
General description of reproductive data.
Width of the bill measured across the widest point at the base.
Length of hallux as measured from base of Digit I on hind limb to base of claw.
The number of individual organisms represented by the catalog record.
Lustre (luster; US English) or l is the way light interacts with the surface of a crystal, rock, or mineral.
Measured with calipers from left side to right side in mm or cm. The neck would probably be at the narrowest point.
Length of plastron.
Length from the top of the upper mandible to the base of the lower mandible measured at the deepest point, either at the bill base or gonys.
The date the specimen ceased to grow and change, as opposed to the date when it was collected.  Often the date of death. Avoid this in favor of additional specimen_event determinations.
Total length of the item.
Free-text description of species associated with the specimen.
A measurement of the female reproductive cell, or gamete.
Archaeological features such as a fire pit, hearth, house foundation, etc. Something that a person made but then left behind at an archaeological site.
Verbatim description of the anatomical location of the parasite in or on the host.
Length of the middle toe as measured from base of Digit III on hind limb to base of claw.
A brief statement indicating how the work came into the current or an earlier collection or how it came to be on view at the repository.
A measurement of the width of the head taken at the widest part of the head.

Length of the smallest individual in a lot of fish measured from the tip of the
snout to the end of the last vertebra or posterior end of caudal peduncle. Do not use for individuals.

Fork length (FL) is the length of a fish measured from the tip of the snout to the end of the middle caudal fin rays and is used in fishes in which it is difficult to tell where the vertebral column ends. It is also considered a more suitable measurement for fish with forked caudal fins.

In fish length of the largest individual in a lot measured from the tip of the
snout to tip of the longest lobe of caudal fin. Measurement done with
caudal fin lobes compressed and measured at midline. Do not use for individuals.

Chord measurement along the dorsal ridge of the upper mandible from the tip of the bill to the feathering at base of the bill. For birds of prey, culmen length is measured from the tip of the bill to the anterior edge of the cere.

A notation attached to a creative work indicating the copyright owner of a work. The copyright notice may take a variety of forms depending on applicable law. In the United States the most common form is © [year of first publication] [name of copyright holder].
A subjective description of the abundance of organisms, conspecific with the cataloged item, at the collecting locality.
Insufficient documentation DO NOT USE
A free text field describing the development, arrangement, or condition of the teeth or tooth. Specificity, counts, and measurements are encouraged.

Length of the largest individual in a lot of fish measured from the tip of the
snout to the end of the last vertebra or posterior end of caudal peduncle. Do not use for individuals.
General description of fat deposition.
A measure of a bill that should be described in Methods. See also Culmen Length for a more specific term.

In fish length of the smallest individual in a lot measured from the tip of the snout to tip of the longest lobe of caudal fin. Measurement done with caudal fin lobes compressed and measured at midline. Do not use for individuals.

Measured from the bend of the wing to the tip of the longest primary feathers. Often the wings and feathers may be flattened so that the measure is maximized but in some cases the chord length with natural curvature is preferred (note in Methods).
Text of a label describing the object when exhibited in a museum or other public space.

Frame rate (commonly expressed in frames per second or FPS) is typically the frequency at which consecutive images are captured or displayed. This definition applies to film and video cameras, computer animation, and motion capture systems.
A measurement of eggshell thickness generally representing the average thickness gauged at both poles and equator.
The attribute value was not detected.
Carapace length measured as straight line across curved surface.
A measure of the width of the tail at the location where the tail meets the torso.
Number of eggs belonging to avian nest parasite (e.g., cowbird).
Dimensions of the object (height x width x depth).
Number of eggs laid in a discrete group within a clearly defined, often elaborate, nest. (after "A Dictionary of BIRDS", edited by Bruce Campbell and Elizabeth Lack, 1985)
Identified compound present in a given mixture, using the thin-layer chromatography technique.
Inscriptions and or marks found on the object.
Keywords relevant to the object. Mainly used for migration from legacy database, i.e., exists in an older database, may be discarded later.
Indigenous language term for a given object and/or material type.
General description of the stage of development of the egg or embryo within the egg.
A measure of the full circumference of the tail at the location described in method.
General description of the bursa.
Is an item historical (vs. ethnological)?
The abundance of certain stable isotopes and chemical elements within organic and inorganic compounds.
Dietary contents contained in the crop of birds.
Cultural affiliation of object creator.
Standard measurement for bats.

Information about the presence of and/or general description of a featherless, fluid-filled area on the abdomen or breast of birds that is filled with surface blood vessels which are used to apply heat to the eggs during incubation.
A description of the nest itself (e.g., "Nest is a small cup made of grasses"), not the placement (e.g., 6 ft in willow tree) which should go into habitat.
The general location within an archaeological site where an object was collected.
Comments about timing of nest building and egg laying.
Length of a spur of cartilage and/or bone arising from inner side of ankle and running along part of outer interfemoral membrane in bats.
Age derived from radioisotope methodology.
Title of the object that may be different from the title used in Identification.
Sex of the organism.

The subject matter of a work of art (sometimes referred to as its content) is the narrative, iconographic, or non-objective meaning conveyed by an abstract or a figurative composition. It is what is depicted in and by a work of art. It also covers the function of an object or architecture that otherwise has no narrative content. Formerly subject, a topic of the resource.
Archaeological test unit an object was collected from.
Length from tip of the snout to the most posterior opening of the cloacal slit (vent), commonly used in herpetology. Best practice will include means of measurement in Methods.

Standard Length (SL) is the length of a fish measured from the tip of the
snout to the end of the last vertebra or posterior end of caudal peduncle.
natural stratigraphic layer an archaeological object was collected from
Is there any reason that this organism and its host do not represent a natural occurence?
Length of spleen; abnormal size may be a marker of infection or pregnancy.
Internal information of any sort. Do not change privacy setting!
Parasite host's sex as recorded by collector or preparator.
Monetary value.
Depth under the ground surface; free-text field.
A number that represents the number of pairs of homologous copies of each chromosome that are present.
The exact north coordinate within an archaeological site where an object was collected.
The exact east coordinate within an archaeological site where an object was collected.

A portfolio is a number of prints presented as a group and often, though not necessarily, by the same artist and based on a related theme. A series can be defined as more than one related work grouped by the artist or in some logical way. Use if there is a title for the portfolio or series.
Length of carapace, straight or curved not specified.
A value that represents the number of labels associated with the object.

The quadrant within an archaeological test unit where an object was collected from. During an archaeological excavation test units are split into four equal quads and then each quad is excavated separately.
Parasite host's age as described by collector or preparator.
Materials used in the construction of the object. (These data will be normalized and standardized as cultural collection development continues.)
The means that resulted in or contributed to the death of the cataloged organism, and may include the circumstances of the act that produced any such fatal injuries.
Antler diameter at the lowest point on the antler beam, above the burr.
A general description of the condition of the tail.
Description or degree of skull pneumaticity.
The description of the host's taxonomic identity exactly as provided by the original documentation of the specimen. These will vary from explicit scientific names to vague common names.

Total number of points on one (method = left or right) or both (method = total) antlers that are at least 1” in length, including the tips of the beams. Total, left, or right should be included in method to provide details about what the count describes.
Length of the ear from the notch to the tip.
Antler circumference at the lowest point on the antler beam, above the burr.

Verbatim agent accepts any string value. This attribute should be used when there is little to no information about a collector or preparator instead of creating a low-information agent (no dates, relationships, or addresses are known for the agent). Indicate the agent role with regard to the catalog object in the attribute method.
The record was not examined for the given value.
General description of molt stage or condition.
Describes the rights of the copyright holder listed for the object.
Height of the specimen.
Maximum chord length of the head along the dorsal midline, measured from the tip of the rostrum to the back of the head.
Length of the hind foot from the back of the ankle to the tip of the longest claw. A numeric value plus units.

Virulence gene index refers to multi-virulence gene index, MVGI (the number of virulence genes detected in one strain/total number of detected virulence genes) and is recorded as a ratio of the number of virulence genes expressed in the specimen (see Deng et al 2020). Pathogenic bacteria virulence genes are specific genetic components that enable bacteria to cause disease by enhancing their ability to invade host tissues, evade the immune system, and obtain nutrients from the host. These genes encode various factors such as toxins, adhesion molecules, and enzymes that contribute to the bacteria’s pathogenicity. (example of values: 4/5; 5/5; 3/7) Method and date is needed for each entry.
Language of record as registered on Glottolog.
Total duration of an audiovisual item as expressed in minutes and seconds. For example: 148 minutes
Measurement of the short axis of the gonad (testis in males; ovary in females). The side measured (left or right) should be indicated in the Methods if known.

Measurement of the long axis of the gonad (which may be testes or ovary and can be indicated in Remarks or by implication of attribute of sex). Left or right side gonad should be indicated in the Methods.
General description of body condition.
Length measurement of the tarsus. Birds: Chord length of the tarsometatarsus, measured from the back of its articulation with the tibiotarsus to the base of the toes on the top of the foot.
a measurement of the tranverse width: the maximum distance between the medial and lateral surfaces of the tooth.
Length of the forelimb between the elbow and wrist.
The length of the first digit (pollex) of the mammalian forelimb, with claw (e.g. for bats)
anteroposterior tooth length, a measurement of the maximum distance between the anterior and posterior surfaces of the tooth.
Width of the specimen or object.
A systematic examination for the attribute value was made.
Age of specimen given as a numeric value plus units.
The distance from one wingtip to the other wingtip.

All of the fish of any species or population hatched during one annual spawning period, with members of the same year class generally treated as if they were hatched on the same day for analytical purposes.
The developmental stage of the life cycle of the organism represented.

The length of time or stage or state that an organism has lived or an object has existed. This is a free text field so specificity is recommended. If general age groups are desired (e.g., adult, juvenile, subadult, etc), please see life stage and its values. If specific numeric age is known, use numeric age.
Length of tail.
General description of colors.
Text regarding measurements of the specimen (usually biological individual). Use more specific attributes when possible.

The group of individuals within the same species of social insects that have a different appearance. This appearance is usually related to the role of that caste within the colony. Values are controlled by the Caste Code Table.
Cultural affiliation of object user.
Provides information about when and how a cataloged item was processed or handled (inventoried, cataloged, verified, etc.).
The circumference measured around the body directly subordinate to the limbs at the site of the axillaries (e.g., armpits).
Length measurement of the bursa. Specify means of measurement in Methods.
General description of the specimen's gut contents.

Measurement from the crown of head to the crown of the rump in a fetus. It is also possible to use curvilinear length when a linear measurement is not possible, as with a frozen carcass, which mirrors the traditional total length measurement (nose to tail tip).
Description of the object, specimen, or observation.
The attribute value was detected.
Length of the hind foot from the back of the ankle to the base of the longest claw. A numeric value plus units.
Measured with calipers from left side to right side in mm or cm, at the widest point of the body (e.g., belly).
Carapace length measured across curved surface.
The body temperature of an animal.
The way in which an animal acts in response to a particular situation or stimulus.
Total body or object weight.

The values entered in this attribute should represent structured data about a catalog record that does not fit into an existing attribute. Over time, use of structured terms may result in creation of a new attribute if the community deems it valuable. If units are required, they should be part of the free-text structure.
Width of the bill measured at the anterior margin of the nares.
Distance between antlers. Method should be given. For example, "measurements per: https://www.boone-crockett.org/scorechart/add/whitetail_deer."

metadata.description: Record Attributes are descriptive characteristics or metadata about cataloged items (e.g., measurements, subject, lifestage, etc).
